judge_reason: Only the golden share and 100,000 jobs are met. The announcement date, Burritt's framing, the $14B pledge, the $4B mill and the Western PA focus are missing; extra post-closing claims fall outside the official text.
All six yearly ARM figures and the flat 2022-2024 trend are correct, but the answer omits the ~2.8% annual 2019-2022 growth and the ad-plan explanation.
The model correctly states a beat of 80 bps from the low end and 70 bps from the high end.
All four quarterly guidance ranges and their midpoint percentages match the official answer exactly.
All eight official 2024 nominees are named. The opening framing about no new nominees and the extra Mark Finn detail fall outside the official text and do not contradict it.
Amazon is correctly identified and the AMZN/GOOG initial guidance matches, but the Meta $70–72B range excludes the official $62.5B and contradicts the official answer.
Correct CFO named; the extra claims (CFO since March 2024, prior VP Finance role) are outside the official answer and do not affect the grade.
The model commits to a $3.30B total ($3.25B base + $50M adjustment) rather than the official $3.25B total; it is an explicit different value, not a rounding.
Correctly states a 140bps beat; the extra claim that 26.9% is '20 bps above the top' of a 24.0–27.0% range is wrong and self-contradictory, but it falls outside the official answer.
Both revenue figures are pure roundings of the official values, and the 22.6% CAGR matches.
Class C and H are correct, but the Class A and B counts come from a later filing and do not match the official figures.
Inputs and estimates are correct, but using a 32.8 rate gives a 'beat low end' / -1.0% conclusion instead of the official -1.2% miss, and no NT$ guidance is given.
The model states the exact official total of $2,263,113; the stray tool-artifact text at the start does not affect the grade.
The 2023/2024 margins and the trend match, but the 2022 FCF margin is stated as ~224% versus the official 24.8%, which triggers contradiction.
All official inputs, the average inventory and the 6.55x turnover match; the extra alternative and depreciation remarks do not contradict the official answer.
All key terms are correct, but the answer omits that there is no optional redemption by KKR.
All three take rates match (13.3/13.5/13.6%), and the model describes small year-over-year increases consistent with the official trend.
Correctly identifies Gross Revenue Retention Rate and gives the full official definition; extra details are outside the official answer and unverified.
Correct three-year total ($85,002K) and percentage (51.3%); the alternative 58.2% figure is noted but explicitly not adopted.
Both rates and the 410bps increase match the official answer; the extra provision details are outside the rubric.
The answer states the single North American processing vendor and its backup arrangements; the extra bank sponsor detail is outside the official answer.
All three per-night GBV figures are nearby precise values, not roundings of the official $160.44/$163.51/$166.23, so they contradict the official answer.
Model states the 2025 production expectation; its mention of the November 2024 opening is a later revision that does not deny that expectation.
The model states the official $7.5 billion face value excluding sustainability notes; the extra breakdown does not contradict the official answer.
Covers privacy laws, product changes, money transmitter licensing and cybersecurity compliance, but omits the third-party breach and trust/client-retention risks.
Gives 102,000/228,000 ≈ 44.7%, a more precise value that rounds to the official 45%; inputs match the official answer.
Amount, series and final maturity are correct, but the answer omits the 2057 scheduled maturity and all redemption terms.
The model's $14,426,266 thousand matches the official $14,426,266,000 after unit conversion.
All 16 KPIs match the official answer after equivalent unit conversions (thousands, cents, percent); the extra held-for-sale note does not conflict.
The model gives 85,945 thousand (about 85.9M) if-converted shares, a pure rounding of 85,945,127; the extra make-whole caveat is noted but does not change the grade.
Model commits to ~$375M (alternative ~$331M) for 2026 gross profit instead of the official $467M.
Both the purchase and refinance nine-month figures match the official answer exactly, in thousands.
Model gives a $1.6B impact and 13.7% decrease (pre-tax, on year-end debt), versus the official $1.261B and 10.7%.
States 20% of FY2024 revenue from channel partners; the extra dollar figures and prior-year shares are outside the official answer and do not affect the grade.
The line item (stock-based compensation) is correct, but the stated $1.879B is not a rounding of the official $1.935B, so it fails and contradicts the official answer.
Per-share price, equity value and enterprise value are correct, but the 0.7926 exchange ratio is missing.
The model states the official $4.7 billion cumulative Merger restructuring cost as of Dec 31, 2024, and its extra context does not conflict with it.
Correctly says beat, but 25 bps (from rounded margins) is not a rounding of the official 26.1 bps.
Correctly lists the quarterly revenue growth, operating margin and EPS guidance and the full-year FCF and gross leverage guidance, but describes full-year EPS as a level rather than YoY growth.

All seven official adjustments are listed with equivalent descriptions. The extra earlier-filing items and the dubious, unlabeled reconciliation table fall outside the official text and do not contradict it.
Correctly states the Q4 2024 comparable store sales decline of 0.8% (-0.8%). The extra claims (net sales, store counts, Q1/Q3/FY comps) are outside the official text and were not graded.
KO and PEP match, but KDP is given as ~85% instead of 0.83 (contradiction), and KHC and SJM are omitted in favor of different peers.
Take rates, growth figures and the volume-driven conclusion are correct, but the Mobility, Delivery and Freight segment growth rates are omitted.
Model gives exactly 3.3 nights per booking for Asia Pacific in 2024. The extra regional figures fall outside the official answer and do not affect the grade.
Stated $1,407 million SBC add-back for 2024 matches official $1,407,000,000; extra 2023 comparison is outside the official text and not graded.
All three acquisitions are correct, but the model says Residential and Mortgages revenue grew, which misses the official decline and triggers contradiction.
The answer gives a 7.4% MISS, matching the official figure and direction; its supporting guidance and actual figures fall outside the official text and were not graded.
IFP, GEP, revenue and EBITDA are correct, but SBC and capex are called 'in line' instead of above/below expectation, and weighted shares are omitted.
Figures and ranges are all correct, but the answer concludes General Mills beat guidance in both FY2023 and FY2024, contradicting the official FY2024 'met expectations'.
Model graded later periods (Q4 2025–Q3 2026) instead of the official Q1–Q4 2024, so no figure matches and its 5.9% average contradicts the official 2.2%.
